dataset.source: PhysioNet Sudden Cardiac Death Holter Database (sddb), record 30

transition_label.meaning: elapsed time from record start to onset of sustained ventricular fibrillation

extraction_path.reason: wfdb.rdann('30', 'ari', pn_dir=None) on the locally downloaded .hea/.ari pair succeeded on first attempt and returned 131512 annotations with fs=250 Hz consistent with the header -- no fallback to raw ECG voltage (Priority 2) was needed.
extraction_path.method: RR-interval series (standard cardiac HRV / critical-slowing-down series per Peng et al., Ivanov et al.), NOT raw ECG voltage. beat_time_sec = annotation_sample / fs (250 Hz). RR_i = beat_time[i+1] - beat_time[i], in seconds, taken in chronological order.

annotation_filtering.rationale: Looked up each symbol's official MIT-BIH ecgcodes.h category via wfdb.io.annotation.ann_label_table: '+' = Rhythm change (label_store 28) and 's' = ST change (label_store 18) are both NON-BEAT annotations (they mark rhythm/ST-segment events, not a QRS complex location) and would corrupt the RR series if left in (an RR 'interval' spanning a non-beat mark is not a real cardiac cycle length). All other symbols present (N=normal, S=supraventricular premature, r=R-on-T PVC, V=premature ventricular contraction, E=ventricular escape, '?'=beat not classified during learning) are genuine beat-location annotations per the same table and were KEPT. This is a simple, standard, table-driven filter (not a hand-tuned or invented one). Ectopic/abnormal beats (S, V, r, E) were deliberately NOT removed beyond this: excluding them would require an interpolation/NN-interval scheme, which is exactly the kind of extra methodological judgment call the task instructed against inventing, and since ectopic burden is itself expected to rise approaching a VF transition, removing it risks removing part of the physiological signal being tested rather than removing noise.

not_filtered_but_noted.issue: 36 of 35382 RR intervals in the primary segment (0.09%) exceed 2 seconds (max 10.68 s), most likely brief automatic-detector dropouts (signal quality loss) rather than true beats; a few could be genuine sinus pauses, which are also a plausible pre-VF phenomenon. These were left in unfiltered, per the same reasoning above (no complex artifact-rejection scheme invented post hoc) and are logged here as a known limitation.

primary.definition: All RR intervals from record start (elapsed 00:00:00) up to the last beat at or before vfon elapsed time (07:54:33 = 28473 s).
primary.total_duration_hms: 07:54:31.772 (sum of RR intervals; 1.228 s short of the 07:54:33 vfon mark because the segment necessarily ends at the last detected beat at/before that instant)

robustness.definition: The 50% most recent RR intervals (by sample count) of the primary segment -- i.e. the second half, closest to VF onset.
